scenario: A proposed Android torrent client must download into the user's explicitly selected folder. A prior regular file has the same exact payload relative path. What is the default engineering response?

choices.text: Ban all existing paths and implement a custom JNI disk writer
Use documented libtorrent check/reuse/replace of that authorized regular payload with path containment and real-byte tests
Silently delete the entire folder before download

reason: authorized ordinary same-path payload differs from non-owned exports

scenario: A ZIP exporter gets a returned SAF URI that might identify an existing unrelated document. Earlier code opens it in truncating write mode. How should shipping proceed?

choices.text: Treat picker selection as permission to truncate any URI
Permit export after one JVM-only mock test
Keep unsafe exporter refused, implement a provider-specific new-object positive path and separately reviewed exact-target Replace

reason: document target identity and consent are necessary

scenario: A remote rTorrent endpoint returns public version and inventory to supplied invented credentials. The test says 'authenticated'. What do you fix?

choices.text: Require challenged/accepted credentials in test AND shipping Android Connect before persisting identity
Keep Connect behavior because public success implies credential validity
Add a second anonymous version read as authentication evidence

reason: transport authentication must be actually challenged

scenario: Repeated native resume metadata events grow unbounded. Which correction is proportional?

choices.text: Extend unlimited event files until disk fills
Prove conventional bounded transactional storage, atomic migration, retirement and real restart/Remove tests
Rewrite all torrent payload writers and default Downloads

reason: metadata durability is separate from payload policy

scenario: Exclusive CREATE_NEW file publication prevents overwrites but the app can die during the streaming copy before Room admission. What follows?

choices.text: Automatically delete any unknown same-hash path
Treat atomic creation as proof of an atomic complete file
Journal ownership and crash boundaries, preserve or quarantine ambiguous bytes and verify a safe recovery path

reason: no-replace does not imply complete-file visibility

scenario: A CI job verifies old/new APK migration with one ephemeral signer inside a single run, but production debug builds have different certificates. Can app updates be called safe?

choices.text: No: owner-stable signing and real across-build populated adb install -r still need proof
Yes: shared temporary test key is sufficient forever
Yes: tell the user to uninstall first

reason: temporary signer cannot prove owner signing continuity

scenario: WallpaperManager.setBitmap entered, then threw/cancelled. A new rotation might apply again. Correct response?

choices.text: Clear pending and retry immediately
Mark definite failure and advance shuffle bag
Persist pending/uncertain, pause auto-repeat and only reconcile from trustworthy OS evidence

reason: non-idempotent side-effect uncertainty

scenario: The screenshot atlas CI is green, but at 320dp/200% text the app title wraps one letter per line. What next?

choices.text: Inspect specific capture and fix actual adaptive Compose layout; recheck exact visual viewport
Accept because capture generated successfully
Remove 200% text test

reason: visual acceptance requires actual screenshot inspection

scenario: API35 UI test failed to find DocumentsUI, but logcat shows system PickActivity and no Copy occurred. What is the first classification?

choices.text: Proven broken SFTP byte engine
Pre-transfer OS picker/harness-window or reachability failure needing real window diagnostics
Successful copy because the intent was sent

reason: last reached step is pre-transfer picker visibility

scenario: A new Copy UI opened two Android picker intents then displayed Success without reading output bytes. Is E2 acceptance earned?

choices.text: Yes, UI progression proves transfer
Yes, if source is synthetic
No: require real two-authority grants, confirmed target membership and independently read-back bytes and source preservation

reason: picker intent is not a write receipt

scenario: A native file is renamed out of an Android directory. GitHub's workflow-level paths filter prevents the native selector from running. Best fix?

choices.text: Cheap always-dispatched, trusted-base selector that examines old/new paths, fails closed and preserves required check contexts
Tell the selector to process renames only if the workflow runs
Disable native checks on renamed files

reason: a skipped top-level workflow cannot self-detect

scenario: A PR text says 'do not close #143' but GitHub closes the issue on merge. How to prevent recurrence?

choices.text: Disable all issue links in PRs
Use 'Issue #143 remains open' for incomplete work, reserve auto-close syntax for completion and check post-merge issue state
Pretend issue closure proves implementation

reason: parser acts on negated keywords

scenario: Stop is requested while an underlying input stream is blocking. It returns bytes after coroutine cancellation. How prevent a false VERIFIED result?

choices.text: Check owning Job/permit after every blocking boundary, before writes and after readback EOF; retain uncertainty if side effect possible
Ignore stop once stream started
Mark verified when the progress UI disappears

reason: cancellation is not retroactive to blocking calls

scenario: Two old green stacked PRs have different base trees and partial overlapping fixes; latest main differs. How integrate?

choices.text: Merge both because each was green
Close one as superseded without comparing unique tests
Reconcile unique source/test deltas against live main, build one final integrated head and rerun required checks

reason: stale-parent green is not final-head proof

scenario: The app receives an Android Photo Picker result while another import is busy. Current handler clears the result before admission. Next step?

choices.text: Persist the temporary URI in public preferences for later
Only clear after admitted; otherwise retain visible transient retry/dismiss, with repick after process loss
Drop result silently to avoid duplicate content

reason: do not lose user intent or persist unsafe provider grant

scenario: A 12-file SAF Copy batch is reviewed once. After 6 verified items, item 7 is uncertain. What should the app report?

choices.text: Success 12/12 because batch was authorized
Rollback by deleting all source files
Stop without blind replay, keep sources, show 6 verified and item 7 uncertain with per-item journal

reason: batch review does not imply atomicity

scenario: A chained installed API35 lifecycle job confirms real dataSync timeout and cold restore, then stops logging just after reboot is armed and the run times out. What validation decision is justified?

choices.text: Declare all four chained lifecycle scenarios passed because the first phase did
Keep the real reboot gate red; retain independent FGS-positive evidence and add bounded ADB stages and step receipts before rerunning only the unresolved phase
Replace the reboot test with mocked ADB and declare E2 accepted

reason: shared sessions need independently observable bounded phases; probable hanging command is not yet proven

scenario: A repeated genuine Android picker-and-Copy test has independently verified target bytes, untouched source and visible success, but consistently fails during Material3 Compose teardown. Which check should be prioritized during diagnosis?

choices.text: Run the full two-picker copy repeatedly without changing the failure hypothesis
Waive the teardown exception and merge because the bytes are correct
Keep end-to-end lifecycle qualification open, isolate minimal Activity/semantics/picker conditions first, then rerun one complete exact-head E2 after the proposed fix

reason: diagnostic information gain is distinct from final end-to-end acceptance

scenario: A real installed magnet test sees expected verified destination bytes but zero received new bytes; the destination had already completed that exact public torrent. What should happen?

choices.text: Report fresh peer ingress because the destination SHA matched
Mark fresh-ingress evidence inconclusive, preserve the pre-existing torrent, and use strictly owned alternative fixtures with initial-state and delta assertions
Delete the pre-existing external payload without consent, then retry the same magnet

reason: a complete existing fixture is not proof of newly received peer bytes

scenario: An Android JVM suite runs 1,178 tests, but one Compose assertion times out while waiting simultaneously for background list loading and UI statuses. How best increase the evidence value?

choices.text: Separate exact callback completion from rendered status waits and assert both, preserving existing negative assertions
Treat the whole app as confirmed broken because the full foundation job is red
Delete the UI assertion because 1,178 passing tests are more than enough

reason: a discriminating test separates asynchronous scheduling from UI behavior
